newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Demonstrators picket HK leadership meeting.
newsitem.headline: Demonstrators picket HK leadership meeting.

text.p: Demonstrators brandishing banners in support of jailed Chinese dissidents picketed a historic meeting on Friday of an electoral college charged with selecting Hong Kong's first post-colonial leaders.
Police bundled the protesters away from the entrance ahead of the arrival of China's Foreign Minister Qian Qichen, making his first trip to the British colony to preside over the meeting.

The 400-member Selection Committee formed under Beijing's tight rein will be inaugurated in Hong Kong and begin a month-long mission to select Hong Kong's future leader and the 60 members of a replacement legislature.
"Free Wang Dan, release Wei Jingsheng, oppose the provisional legislature," the small but noisy group of demonstrators chanted as delegates arrived in buses.

Chinese dissident Wang Dan was sentenced on October 30 to 11 years in prison for plotting to overthrow the government and a decision was expected on Friday on his appeal. Wei, often referred to as the "father of the Chinese democracy movement", is now serving a 14-year sentence.
Many of the demonstrators had spent the night on a protest fast outside the building.
Hong Kong's pro-democracy lobby has attacked the process and refused to take part in the selection committee which they have branded as undemocratic.
They are adamantly opposed to China's plan to dissolve the elected legislature and replace it with an interim provisional chamber until new elections are staged.
"The provisional legislature is a great step backwards for democracy," one banner said.

The Selection Committee is due to hold a first round of voting on Friday to narrow the race for the candidate to step into the shoes of colonial governor Chris Patten when British rule draws to a close at midnight on June 30 next year.
To enter the final run-off for the job, a candidate must be nominated by at least 50 members of the committee.
The Selection Committee meets again on December 11 to pick the winner.
Two business magnates and two former judges are regarded as the frontrunners in the race.
